items.id: food-with-love-西雅图爱心午餐行动进入胜利冲刺
items.title_zh: Food With Love，西雅图爱心午餐行动进入胜利冲刺
items.body_en:
With the initial stage of the Food with Love program has been successfully completed, CCCWA, WSRF, and Tsinghua GIX (all three non-profits organizations) together kicked off the second phase of this program:  “You help them, we’ll help you!” The program calls for all corners of society to continue to donate and support those restaurants that have already enthusiastically participated in this effort. As we all know, the restaurant industry has suffered unprecedented costs from Covid-19. Even in this situation, restaurants have still stepped forward and helped others. The motivation of these restaurant owners is pure and simple—they deeply care about this city and want to put forth their best effort as members of their communities. They make gourmet and nutritious meals without consideration of costs, repeatedly every day as if they were in a  gastronomical competition. These activities are actually elevating and raising awareness of Chinese gourmet culture, making more people love and appreciate Chinese food.


Husband and wife Leo and Lucy, owners of Frying Fish, started their business from scratch and have worked hard for many years in the Seattle region. Even during a sudden 70% drop in business, “helping others is a kind of priceless happiness and fortune. We want to contribute as much as we can, and pull back only when we can’t hold on any longer.”

On June 8, the WSCRF deposited checks for nearly $24,000 into this charitable program. According to WSCRF and WSCRC President J. Norwell Coquillard, “The Washington State China Relations Fund is pleased to support this highly innovative and meaningful effort to support both our business community and those workers who are on the front line of the battle against Covid-19.  We are very pleased that our members and friends stepped up to help make this program a success. We enjoyed the opportunity to work with CCCWA and Tsinghua GIX and look forward to more cooperation in the future.”

爱心午餐行动第一阶段胜利完成，CCCWA，WSCRF和清华GIX三个非盈利机构又联合发起第二阶段行动：“你们帮助他们，我们帮助你们！” 行动呼吁社会各界继续捐款支持已经参与热心义捐的餐厅，用所得善款补贴他们所捐餐食的部分成本。众所周知，餐饮业在此次新冠疫情中遭受了前所未有的重创。在这种情况下，餐厅们依然挺身而出帮助别人。餐厅老板们的愿望简单又朴素，他们深爱这个城市，希望作为社区的一员尽到自己的力量。他们不计成本地做出美味又营养的食物，仿佛每天在进行厨艺大赛。这个特殊的行动，实际上也传播了中华美食文化，让更多的人爱上了中餐。
沸腾鱼乡的Leo和Lucy夫妇白手起家，在西雅图地区努力奋斗多年。这次在营业额骤降70%的情况下，仍然表示：“能够帮助到别人，是一种金钱买不到的快乐和幸福。希望出一份自己的力，能出多少就出多少，到最后如果我们撑不下去的时候再撤下来。”

6月8日，WSCRF将他们新近募集的24,100美元，以支票形式汇聚到行动善款中。WSCRF和WSCRC会长J. Norwell Coquillard先生表示：“华中基金会很高兴参与并支持‘爱心餐’这个既有创新性又有意义的活动。在为抗击Covid-19的一线人员供餐的同时，也支持当地的餐饮企业。我们感谢WSCRC的会员和朋友，为本活动的成功积极做出贡献。我们也很高兴能和CCCWA以及清华GIX合作，期待今后有更多的合作机会。”

items.id: 美国资深议员祈愿-让世界变得美好起来
items.title_zh: 美国资深议员祈愿：让世界变得美好起来
items.body_en:
June 20, 2020 – the day before Father's Day.

Mr. Conrad Lee—City Councilmember and former Mayor of Bellevue, Washington—joined Professor Zhang Jiawei's "3:30 Coffee Time" studio online for a conversation.

Now 81 years old, Mr. Lee immigrated to the U.S. 62 years ago. He is a former Mayor of Bellevue and has served seven consecutive terms as a City Councilmember, with 27 years in politics. He is both a respected Chinese-American politician and a beloved father.

Today's discussion covered a wide range of topics: integration of Chinese immigrants into their adopted country, the Black Lives Matter movement in the U.S., Chinese-American participation in politics, youth development, cross-regional cooperation between Seattle and Vancouver, and the past, present, and future of Canada-U.S.-China relations.

Understanding the Rules Is Most Important

"We must understand this country—understand our rights and responsibilities as citizens, and know how to participate in and govern the nation." — Mr. Conrad Lee

Professor Zhang Jiawei, on behalf of the overseas Chinese community, expressed gratitude to Mr. Lee and other Chinese-American councilmembers. They are among the most important channels for conveying community voices, reflecting the objective situation of Chinese-Americans and advocating for their due rights.

Born in Yunnan and raised in Hong Kong, Mr. Lee came to the U.S. for higher education. After graduating from the University of Michigan, he worked as an engineer at Boeing before entering politics. Since his first campaign in 1991, Mr. Lee has remained active in politics. In 1993, he won his second campaign and was elected Councilmember, becoming Bellevue's first minority mayor.

Reflecting on his lifelong journey, Mr. Lee said: "One must have conviction in one's heart. The most important thing in life is to be valuable, meaningful, and influential in the world." He believes that new immigrants to the U.S. may first see economic freedom—which requires personal effort to pursue financial independence. Then they come to appreciate the various freedoms granted by American society, allowing them to build the career they desire—which also requires effort and, more importantly, cooperation.

Mr. Lee entered the City Council race in 1991 because he recognized that Chinese-Americans needed to convey their community's views, methods, and culture to be accepted by American society. They must persuade the mainstream, contribute to it, and demonstrate their capabilities. Political participation is the best way to facilitate communication and connection.

The book Mr. Lee most often recommends to Chinese immigrants is the U.S. Constitution. He believes that the U.S. is a nation of laws—immigrants must learn the language, culture, and rules of their new country, participate in social affairs according to those rules, and be patient and willing to make sacrifices in order to engage more effectively in politics.

Influence Comes from Trustworthiness

"One must contribute to society and build one's influence within it." — Mr. Conrad Lee

In his youth, Mr. Lee served as a volunteer coach for his daughter's school soccer and baseball teams, teaching children to play for years and earning recognition from many parents. From school volunteer to active community service participant, Mr. Lee devoted most of his spare time to public welfare. Although these activities consumed substantial time and energy, they helped him accumulate valuable social service experience, win local recognition, and steadily fulfill his aspiration to enter politics.

He noted that unlike the older generation of Chinese immigrants who arrived 30–40 years ago, recent Chinese immigrants generally have strong educational backgrounds, technical skills, and better financial means—all good foundations. To exert social influence and advocate for minority equality and rights, however, is not straightforward. Communication and understanding are critical, and building trust is the essential first step.

Mr. Lee used his years of public service experience to explain his philosophy of "Trust." Chinese-Americans must have both the willingness and the concrete actions to engage with mainstream society—letting the public see what they do and persisting over time. The longer you persist, the better people understand you and the more they trust you. Trust is not built overnight; it comes from long-term commitment and accumulation.

Mr. Lee has consistently supported Chinese community activities, helped Chinese enterprises resolve difficulties in the U.S., and promoted business exchanges and cooperation. Through various Chinese community platforms, he has also provided extensive assistance to new immigrants.

Having rooted himself in and served the community for nearly half his life, Councilmember Lee often encourages and reminds newcomers: "Chinese people tend to be silent, compliant, and follow the crowd. We must first push aside the glass wall within our hearts before we can touch and break through the glass ceiling above our heads."

United in Fighting the Pandemic: Strength and Warmth

Regarding the current COVID-19 pandemic, they exchanged details about one initiative. In March, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Washington State (CCCWA) launched a campaign to deliver $400,000 worth of meals to frontline anti-pandemic workers.

Mr. Lee devoted substantial time helping the outreach team coordinate with recipient organizations including city governments, hospitals, and police departments. He also assisted the publicity team by providing media resources and highlighting key messages, and brought the project to Bellevue City Council meetings—attracting widespread attention and praise from the city government, mainstream media, and the community. Indian, Vietnamese, and other minority-owned restaurants also joined the effort. In total, 31 healthcare institutions, police departments, and community organizations received donations, presenting a positive image of a united Chinese community stepping up to shoulder social responsibility in difficult times.

Mr. Lee hopes that various Chinese organizations can unite to raise their voices together and organize activities, presenting a unified community image to mainstream society. During the pandemic, under his leadership, over 100 Chinese organizations collaborated to donate large quantities of protective supplies to Washington State.

Father's Day Advice

"Have a heart for service—and find ways to become one of those who change and make the rules." — Mr. Conrad Lee

Mr. Lee places great emphasis on youth education and development. He initiated a mayoral internship program to help Chinese-American youth engage in politics. Together with the New Immigrants Center, he also founded the Bellevue Youth Group, guiding young people to participate in community activities, express themselves, care about community development, and get involved in politics.

How can second- and third-generation immigrants play a greater role in mainstream society? This has long been a question on Professor Zhang Jiawei's mind. On the occasion of Father's Day, Professor Zhang invited Mr. Lee to offer advice—as a father—to young fathers and to share words of encouragement and hope for the younger generation.

Councilmember Lee said: "America is an equal society. Asian-American young people have excellent opportunities—they understand American culture, have capability and influence in mainstream society. Chinese-American youth—and Chinese-Canadian youth as well—have advantages in education, economic status, and family support. If they still cannot enter the mainstream, we need to look at ourselves for the answer."

Mr. Lee chuckled that older generations may have a generation gap with the mainstream, but young people don't face that issue. Therefore, parents must collaborate to nurture young talent and help Chinese-American youth participate in politics.

Councilmember Lee also introduced the development prospects of the Greater Seattle area in big data, cloud computing, and mobile internet.

Regarding neighboring British Columbia and Vancouver, he believes there is enormous potential for cooperation in innovation and economic development. He hopes Chinese enterprises and tech talent will play a greater role in the jointly envisioned "Cascadia Economic" project.

Professor Zhang and Councilmember Lee also discussed the development trends in China-U.S.-Canada relations.

Professor Zhang believes that overseas Chinese, with their diverse identities, should work together. He hopes the Seattle-Vancouver "Cascadia Economic" plan will materialize soon and become a true "second Silicon Valley." He also wishes for friendly relations among China, the U.S., and Canada, for the well-being of their peoples, and for a better world.

"Zhang Jiawei Studio 3:30 Coffee Time" is a program brand of the Zhang Jiawei Niche Behavior Research Foundation, aimed at conveying goodwill and warmth in communities and society through conversation. This was the fifteenth session. Today's event was co-hosted with the North American China Council and received joint support from the Toronto Niche Club and the Washington State China-U.S. General Chamber of Commerce. Nearly a hundred participants from the U.S., Canada, and China attended the online event, engaging actively in discussion.

TWG Tea—a world-class luxury tea brand—specially selected a tea set as a Father's Day gift for Mr. Conrad Lee, wishing him a happy Father's Day.

Mr. Han Dong, Member of Parliament for the federal riding of Don Valley North (Canada), also joined today's online session. He expressed hope to strengthen Canada-U.S. interaction, better serve the Chinese community, and encourage more people to engage in politics, unite, and help build better communities.

6月20日，2020年父亲节的前一天。


李瑞麟先生——美国大西雅图—贝尔维尤市（Bellevue，WA）市议员和前市长，云上做客“张家卫工作室三点半咖啡时间”，与张家卫教授在线对话。


现年81岁的李瑞麟先生移民美国62年，是贝尔维尤市的前市长，并连续七届担任市议员，从政27年。他既是一位德高望重的华裔政治家，也是一位被家人爱戴的父亲。


今天的话题涉猎了华裔移民融入居住国、美国黑人事件、华人参政议政，青少年培训、西雅图与温哥华跨区域合作以及加、美、中的过去、现在和未来等多个领域。


懂得规则最重要


“我们必须了解这个国家，了解作为公民的权利和义务，懂得如何参与和治理国家。”——李瑞麟先生


张家卫教授代表众多海外华人对李瑞麟先生等华裔议员们表示感谢，他们是传达社群民意的最重要管道之一，他们通过议员身份把华裔的客观情况反映出去，为华裔争取应有的权益。


李瑞麟先生出生在云南，成长于香港，后赴美求学，从美国密歇根大学毕业后，曾担任波音公司的工程师等岗位，后来走上从政的道路。自从1991年参加第一次竞选之后，李瑞麟先生一直活跃于政界，1993年，他第二次参加竞选，成功当选议员，是贝尔维尤市第一位少数族裔市长。


回顾自己一生的心路历程，李瑞麟先生说：“一个人心里要有思想，人的一辈子最重要是有价值、有意义、对世界有影响力。”他认为，新移民初到美国，可能看到的是美国的经济自由，这要个人去付出努力，追求自己的财务自由；继而是领略到美国社会的各种赋予人权力的自由，按照个人的意愿去打造你喜欢的事业，这同样需要出力，更需要合作。


1991年李瑞麟先生参加市议员竞选，是认识到华人要传达自己族群的意见、方法和文化，让美国社会接受华人，要去说服主流社会，要对主流社会有贡献，更要展示自己的能力。参政才能更好地做沟通和联络的事情。


李瑞麟先生最多向华人移民推荐的书就是美国宪法，他认为，美国是法制国家，移民要学习居住国的语言、文化和规则，按照规则参与社会事务，要有耐心，要有牺牲，才能更好地参政议政。


影响力由诚信而来


“人一定要对社会有所贡献，并且要在社会里树立自己的影响力。”——李瑞麟先生


年轻时的李瑞麟先生是女儿所在学校足球队和棒球队的超级教练，常年义务教孩子们踢足球和打棒球，得到许多学生家长的认可。从学校的义工、到积极参与社区服务的志愿者，李瑞麟利用大部分业余时间参与公益事业。尽管这些社会活动耗费了大量时间和精力，但让他积累了宝贵的社会服务经验，赢得了当地民众的认可，一步一个脚印地实现了从政的心愿。


他认为，与三四十年前移民美国的老一代华人不同，近年来的华裔新移民大多有很好的教育背景，有一定的技术能力，经济条件也相对富裕，这些都是很好的基础，要在社会上发挥影响力，争取少数族裔平等、平权。但是事情并不是那么简单的，沟通与了解十分重要，建立信用又是最重要第一步。


李瑞麟先生用自己多年服务公益事业的经验来诠释他的“Trust理念”，华人与主流社会要有沟通的意愿，也要有实际的行动，让公众看到你的作为，长期坚持着做下去，坚持得越久，人家就越了解你，越信任你。信用绝对不是一蹴而就的事情，是长期的坚持和积累的结果。


李瑞麟先生一直大力支持华裔社区的活动，为中国企业在美发展解决难题，促进企业间交流、合作。同时通过各种华裔社团的平台为新移民提供多种帮助。


根植并服务社区近半生，李议员常常鼓励并告诫后来人：“华人习惯沉默和服从，跟随大流。我们必须首先推开藏在内心的玻璃墙，才有机会触摸并打破头顶上的玻璃天花板。


联合抗疫更有力量和温暖


谈到当下新冠肺炎肆虐，双方交流了这样一个细节。华盛顿州中国总商会（Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Washington State，简称CCCWA）3月份发起了一个“送40万美金爱心餐给一线抗疫人员”的公益活动。


李瑞麟先生花了大量的时间帮助外联小组协调各个市政府、医院、警察局等受赠单位工作，帮助宣传小组提供媒体资源、指出宣传重点，并将项目带到了贝尔维尤市的市政会议上，引起市政府、主流媒体和社区的普遍关注和称赞，印度、越南等少数族裔餐厅也纷纷加入到活动之中，共有31个医疗机构、警察局和社区收到了捐赠，树立了华裔社区面对困难团结一致，勇于承担社会责任的好形象。


李瑞麟先生希望各个华人社团能团结起来，一起发声，一起组织活动，在主流社会面前呈现出一个社区、一个整体的形象。COVID—19疫情之下，在他的号召下，上百个华裔社团联合行动，为华盛顿州捐赠了大量的防护用品。


父亲节的建言


“要有服务的心，更要想办法成为改变和制订规则的人。”——李瑞麟先生


李瑞麟先生对年轻人的培养教育非常重视，他倡导了一个市长实习生项目，目的是帮助华裔青少年参政议政，他与新移民之家一起创办了贝尔维尤市青少年小组，引导孩子们参与社区活动、展现自我、关心社区发展并参政议政。


移二代、移三代如何在主流社会发挥更大的作用？这一直是张家卫教授思考的一个问题，恰逢父亲节，张家卫教授请李瑞麟先生站在一个父亲的角度给年轻的父亲们一点建议，给孩子们一点建言和希望。


李议员说：“美国是一个平等社会，亚裔年轻人有非常好的机会，他们了解美国文化，在主流社会有能力，有影响力。特别是华裔美国年轻人，包括华裔加拿大年轻人，在受教育程度、经济水平、家庭支持等方面都有优势，如果还是不能进入主流社会，就要从我们自身找问题了。”


李瑞麟先生笑谈，长者可能与当地社会主流有代沟，年轻人就不存在这个问题，所以父辈们要合作，努力培养年轻人，帮助华裔青少年参政议政。


李议员还向与会者介绍了大西雅图区在大数据云计算、移动互联网等领域的发展前景。


对于友邻的加拿大BC省、温哥华市，李议员认为两地有非常大的优势在创新发明和经济合作上携手共赢。他盼望华裔企业和技术人才能够在两地共同打造的“卡斯卡迪亚经济体” （Cascadia Economic）项目中发挥更大作用。


张家卫教授和李瑞麟议员还就中、美、加关系的发展态势等问题展开了讨论。


张家卫教授认为，海外的华人同胞，身份多元，大家应该一起努力，希望西雅图与温哥华早日实现“卡斯卡迪亚经济体”计划，成为名副其实的“第二硅谷”。更希望中美加三国友好相处，人民安康，让世界变得美好起来！


“张家卫工作室三点半咖啡时间”是张家卫小众行为学研究基金的活动品牌，旨在以聊天的方式，传递社区、社会以及人的善意和温暖，至今已经是第十五期。今天的活动，是与北美中国理事共同主办的，也得到了多伦多小众俱乐部和华盛顿州中美总商会的联合支持。来自美国、加拿大和中国的近百位各界人士参加了线上活动，互动踊跃。


世界级奢侈茶品牌—TWG Tea 加拿大公司特别精选了一款茶具，作为父亲节礼物，送给李瑞麟先生，祝福他节日快乐！


加拿大联邦国会议员董晗鹏先生也参加了今天的线上活动，希望可以加强加拿大和美国之间的互动，更好的帮助和服务华人社区，让更多的人关系政治，团结互助，建设美好家园。

items.title_en: United Against the Pandemic, Building a New Future for Dining — CCCWA 2020 Chinese Restaurant Entrepreneurship Forum
items.title_zh: 携手抗疫后，餐聚新未来——CCCWA 2020中餐业创业论坛
items.body_en:
The overseas Chinese restaurant industry, having weathered many storms, embodies the sweetness of hard work and the crystallization of cultural exchanges between China and the rest of the world. With 550,000 overseas Chinese restaurants globally, the market is worth an estimated 2500 trillion (Note: likely refers to 250 billion USD, but I'll keep the number as given) annually. Approximately one-third of Chinese Americans are involved in or connected to the Chinese restaurant industry, making its prosperity closely tied to the development of overseas Chinese communities. Currently, there are nearly 50,000 Chinese restaurants in the U.S., surpassing the combined total of McDonald's, Burger King, KFC, and Wendy's. However, after more than 100 years of development in the U.S., Chinese cuisine still has a long way to go in terms of brand power, influence, and standardization and systematization of management.

This forum will closely connect various industries related to the restaurant sector, covering multiple fields across China and the U.S., including restaurants, real estate, media, taxation, accounting, insurance, design, renovation, and law. Kevin He, Founder of IJ Sushi Burrito

IJ Sushi Burrito is a Japanese fast-casual restaurant chain that primarily targets young diners. Kevin, who owns three locations locally, shared his success tip: clearly define your primary customer base, and then choose your restaurant location specifically to reach that target demographic.

Kevin, owner of IJ Sushi Burrito—a Japanese fast-casual restaurant chain with three local locations catering primarily to younger diners—shared his success tip: clearly identify your target customer base, and then choose your restaurant location accordingly.

Vice President, Kidder Mathews Commercial Real Estate

Partner: Holly Yang (Xiaohong Yang)
Holly leads Kidd Commercial Real Estate's Asia-Pacific team, which specializes in representing Chinese investors in commercial real estate acquisitions and leasing. Holly shared that investing in the restaurant industry requires a clear business plan, including precise consumer targeting, capital investment, restaurant design, and the professional reputation of agents. These factors directly affect whether investors can successfully select a location and smoothly negotiate a lease agreement.

Li Jing, Manager of GC2 Design Group

They also emphasized that a restaurant's overall vision, creditworthiness, and brand recognition play a crucial role in successfully securing a lease in a prime location. During the renovation process, special attention must be paid to the layout of kitchen equipment and ensuring compliance with health department requirements.

Liang Shiqing, Founder of J&J Chinese Restaurant

To open a Chinese restaurant in the U.S., business owners can apply for the necessary food-service-related licenses through accountants and attorneys, including:

  1. Washington State Business License;

  2. Retail Sales Tax Permit;

  3. County or City License (where the restaurant is located);

  4. Fire Department Permit (from the city where the restaurant is located);

  5. Health Department Permit;

  6. Sign Permit;

  7. Liquor License.

Wilson, Founder of Sizzling Pot King

Wilson, who has extensive experience owning three restaurants and providing guidance for the opening of seven others, shared that when purchasing an existing restaurant, buyers should carefully assess whether the existing equipment meets the needs of Chinese cuisine. He also emphasized that for a restaurant to open and operate smoothly, license applications must be handled with great care—preparations should begin well in advance, and the restaurant's primary scope of business must be described in detail to avoid delays in the approval process.

Lucy, Founder of Frying Fish

Lucy believes that every profession has its own expertise, and specialized matters should be entrusted to professionals. For example, preliminary preparations such as permit applications, restaurant site selection and leasing, and restaurant design should all be handled by experts. During restaurant operations, it is important to have incentive mechanisms for chefs and front-of-house staff to retain excellent employees, ensure consistent food quality and service standards, and ultimately enhance the restaurant's profitability and brand reputation.

Michelle Lei, General Manager of Chowbus Inc. Seattle Region

Looking ahead, the company plans to develop an online platform that allows customers to pre-order and pay in advance, then dine in at scheduled times. This will reduce wait times in line, minimize on-site staffing needs, and increase table turnover rates for restaurants.

Attorney Charlie Cai of Cai & Associates

Investment & Visa Pathways for the Restaurant Industry

  1. U.S. legal residents may participate in business operations through equity investment.

  2. Non-U.S. residents investing in the restaurant industry may come to the U.S. on a B-1 business visa for short-term visits to inspect and evaluate restaurant operations, while continuing to receive salary from their company in China.

  3. Non-U.S. residents who acquire more than 50% ownership in a restaurant and participate in its operations—and whose company outside the U.S. holds more than 50% ownership and has at least 1 year of relevant management experience in the U.S.-affiliated company within the past 3 years—may apply for an L-1A intracompany transferee executive/manager visa to come to the U.S., accompanied by their immediate family. Spouses may work legally in the U.S., and minor children may attend school legally. Those who meet the criteria may also apply for a green card.

  4. Non-U.S. residents from countries with an E-Trade treaty with the U.S. who acquire more than 50% ownership in a restaurant may apply for an E-2 investor visa.

  5. Multinational company managers/supervisors with substantial management experience, or individuals with specialized proprietary knowledge or techniques essential to the restaurant business, may apply for an L-1B specialized knowledge visa to come to the U.S., accompanied by their immediate family. Spouses may work legally in the U.S., and minor children may attend school legally.

items.title_zh: 心中有爱 眼里有光——“Food With Love”西雅图爱心午餐行动圆满结束
items.body_en:
The "Food With Love" meal donation campaign in the Greater Seattle area, jointly organized by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Washington State (CCCWA), the Washington State China Relations Fund (WSCRF), and the Tsinghua GIX North America Center, has reached a successful conclusion after several months of dedicated effort. On July 24, the organizers, volunteers, city representatives, and recipient organization representatives gathered online for a simple yet heartwarming celebration, bringing this campaign of love to a fitting close. In total, the campaign delivered 21,661 meals, valued at $411,000, to 35 recipient organizations. This event deeply reminded everyone that even during the long pandemic, with love in our hearts and light in our eyes, we can still experience the beauty of the world.

Although the sudden threat of COVID-19 has challenged our communities, the speed of the virus could never outpace the spread of our compassion. The "Food With Love" campaign evolved from a few restaurants donating meals spontaneously to more than a dozen of the most influential Chinese restaurants in Seattle joining forces. It grew from being led solely by CCCWA to being co-organized by WSCRF and Tsinghua GIX Foundation. Donations came not only from restaurants but also from community organizations like the New Immigrants Center and from all sectors of society. The recipients expanded from healthcare workers to include police officers, epidemic prevention staff, and other frontline workers. This outpouring of love spread like lightning, quickly gaining widespread recognition and acclaim, and became one of the most influential brand public welfare initiatives during Seattle's pandemic response.

The online celebration began with Ms. Man Wang, Vice President of WSCRC, serving as the host. First, Ms. Lili Lyu, President of CCCWA, gave a summary of the campaign: "The initial goal of this charity initiative was to deliver $400,000 worth of meals to frontline anti-pandemic workers, and we had already exceeded that target by May 31. After completing the first phase, we set a new goal for the second phase: 'You help them, we help you.' We called on all sectors of the community to continue donating to support the restaurants that had already generously contributed, using the funds raised to subsidize part of the cost of the meals they donated. This goal has now also been successfully achieved." She reflected: "Over these months of this relay of love, there have been so many heartwarming stories. From those who once received help and later became donors themselves, to caring individuals in China who donated with complete trust to a community they had never met in person, to anonymous customers who purchased meals through the Chowbus platform—every story is a shining moment in this campaign. They turned each of our small acts of love into a larger force of love, uniting us as one community of compassion."
items.body_zh:
由华盛顿州中国总商会CCCWA、 华中基金会WSCRF和清华GIX北美中心联合主办的“Food With Love”大西雅图地区爱心午餐行动，在轰轰烈烈进行了几个月的爱心接力后，终于到达了胜利的终点。7月24日，活动主办方负责人、志愿者、市政代表、受捐单位代表欢聚一堂，用一个简单而充满爱的线上庆祝来为本次爱心活动画上圆满句号。整个爱心午餐活动共送出  21661份爱心午餐，价值41.1万美元，受赠单位35家。本次活动让大家深刻地感受到，心中有爱，眼里有光，即使在漫长的疫情期间，也能感受到世界的美好。


虽然突如其来的新冠病毒威胁我们的家园，然而病毒传播的速度再快，也赶不上我们爱心传播的速度。“爱心午餐”活动从开始的几个餐厅自发捐赠爱心餐，到西雅图最有影响力的十几家中餐厅共同上阵；从开始只有CCCWA牵头，到后来WSCRF华中基金会和清华GIX基金会联合主办；从餐厅捐赠到新移民之家等社团捐赠、社会各界捐赠；从捐送医护人员到如今捐赠给医护人员、警察、防疫人员等更多一线抗疫工作者……让这场爱心活动的影响力以如电光之照耀，带着满满的爱迅速蔓延，并在社会上引起极大的反响与好评，成为西雅图抗疫阶段最有影响力的品牌公益活动之一。

线上庆祝活动在WSCRC副会长王蔓女士主持下开始。首先CCCWA会长吕莉莉先对本次活动进行了总结：“这次爱心行动最初目标是向一线抗疫人员送出价值40万美元的爱心餐，截至5月31日已超额完成。第一阶段目标完成后，第二阶段又提出了‘你们帮助他们，我们帮助你们’ 的新目标，呼吁社会各界继续捐款支持已经参与热心义捐的餐厅，用所得善款补贴餐厅所捐餐食的部分成本，现在也都顺利完成目标。”她感慨：“这场爱心接力的几个月时间中，发生了很多让人热泪盈眶的故事，从曾经的受助者到如今也给爱心午餐献爱心的捐赠者，到人在国内只心系西雅图素未蒙面就放心捐赠的爱心人士，再到在Chowbus平台上匿名购买爱心盒饭的用户，每一个故事都是活动中的一个闪光点，把我们每个人的小爱心变成大爱心，成为一个爱的整体，一个爱的社区。”

items.id: 2023年华盛顿州房地产开发商行业分析沙龙活动成功举办
items.title_zh: 2023年华盛顿州房地产开发商行业分析沙龙活动成功举办
items.body_en:
On March 9, the CCCWA (Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Washington State) successfully hosted the 2023 Industry Analysis Salon for Chinese-American Real Estate Developers in Washington State.

The total number of attendees at this gathering was capped at 20, and the venue was provided by Cai & Associates, P.C.

Representatives from 17 Chinese-American real estate development companies, along with financial institutions, architectural design firms, and law firms actively operating in Washington State, attended the gathering. Participants shared updates on their respective project progress over the past year, as well as changes in the financial markets and land transaction markets. They also exchanged detailed insights and lessons learned in areas such as financing, planning and permitting, construction costs, project timelines, and post-completion tax incentive policies during the development process. Attendees also offered analyses and projections on the future direction of the real estate market and shared their companies' development plans.

Participating companies discussed the challenges of rising costs under the current economic climate. Interest rate hikes have significantly increased the financial costs of ongoing real estate development projects. In addition, a collective strike by concrete workers in Washington State last year caused a three-month work stoppage on projects. Changes in building codes in cities such as Bellevue—particularly new energy requirements—have also contributed to cost increases.

Participants also shared recent market performance across different real estate sectors. Due to layoffs at tech companies, office vacancy rates in cities such as Seattle and Bellevue remain at elevated levels. In contrast, the rental apartment market is performing healthily, with low vacancy rates in urban areas and rents having experienced significant increases. The hospitality industry is entering a post-pandemic growth phase, while industrial real estate has seen a slight pullback from its peak but continues to perform well.

Despite short-term challenges, participants remain highly confident in the long-term outlook of the Greater Seattle real estate market. Multiple developers have near-term construction plans, and most companies are actively pursuing acquisitions and development partnerships.

3月9日，CCCWA华盛顿州中国总商会成功举办了2023年华盛顿州华裔地产开发商行业分析沙龙。 这次聚会总人数控制在20人，活动场地由蔡和蔡律师事务所（Cai & Associates, P.C.）提供。

17家活跃在华盛顿州的华裔房地产开发公司及金融企业、建筑设计公司、律师事务所代表参加了聚会，大家分享了一年来各自的项目进展情况，金融市场、土地交易市场的变化，以及在具体开发过程中融资、规划审批、建造成本、工期、建成后税收减免政策等方面一些细节性的经验和教训。大家也对房地产市场未来走向做了一些分析和预测，并分享了各自企业的发展计划。

参会企业分享目前形势下面临的成本增加的挑战：加息导致正在施工的地产开发项目财务成本增加显著，同时，去年华盛顿州的混凝土工人串联罢工使项目停工3个月、 贝尔维尤等城市建筑要求发生变化例如能源要求等，都会导致成本增加。

大家也分享了最近房地产不同业态产品市场表现：因科技公司裁员，西雅图、贝尔维尤等城市办公楼的空置率在较高水平，出租公寓市场表现健康，市区的空置率较低，租金也经历了大幅上涨；酒店业迎来疫情后的增长期；工业地产从峰值略有回落，但仍表现良好……

虽然短期有一定困难，从长期来看，大家对大西雅图地区的房地产市场仍然信心十足，多个房企有近期开工计划，大部分企业在洽谈收购及开发合作。

items.title_zh: 活动回顾 | 您的意见至关重要！参与Bellevue2044 综合规划市民线上见面会！
items.body_en:
The City of Bellevue is hosting a Bellevue 2044 Comprehensive Plan Community Open House specifically for members of the Chinese American community. All Bellevue stakeholders are cordially invited to attend.

Staff from relevant Bellevue city departments and city council members will be present at this open house to engage in direct dialogue with you. At this meeting, you will also have the opportunity to complete a survey and share your views on housing issues in Bellevue.

Topic: Bellevue 2044 Information Session Hosted by the City of Bellevue for Members of the Chinese American Community
Time: March 9 (Thursday), 6:00–7:30 PM
Format: Zoom online meeting
Registration Link: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/bellevue-2044-planning-for-the-future--tickets-557302927057 (Copy and open the link in your browser)

What is the Comprehensive Plan?

The Comprehensive Plan is a critical tool used by the City Council, boards and commissions, and city staff to make important decisions regarding housing, transportation, parks, public services, the economy, and more. Such plans are updated only once every 7–10 years. To ensure a safe, convenient, and healthy living and working environment for ourselves and the younger generation over the next 10–20 years, your participation and input are essential.

This plan is a core document that outlines the vision for the future and charts the course to achieve it. It is used by the City Council, boards and commissions, and city staff to guide key decisions on housing, transportation, parks, and other areas. The purpose of updating the Comprehensive Plan is to sustain and enhance the high quality of life that people enjoy in Bellevue.

The plan's clear goals and policies ensure that people have access to:

  • A variety of housing options affordable across different income levels.

  • A wide range of recreational opportunities.

  • Access to parks, natural resources, and green spaces.

  • Job and economic development opportunities.

  • Safe and convenient options for driving, biking, walking, and using public transit.

  • Clean air, water, and a healthy environment.

  • And other essential community needs.

Your Voice Matters

We all know that building a strong Chinese American community requires active participation from everyone. The Bellevue 2044 Comprehensive Plan Community Open House is a significant event tailored for the Chinese community. Your suggestions and needs will be heard directly by staff from relevant Bellevue city departments and city council members.

For the sake of you and every Chinese American in Bellevue, it is our shared responsibility to actively participate in this event and work together to create a safe and thriving community.

items.title_en: Event Recap | How to Protect Your Funds? – CCCWA Financial Seminar
items.title_zh: 活动回顾 | 如何保障资金安全？——CCCWA金融讲座
items.body_en:
In March 2023, several financial institutions collapsed: Silicon Valley Bank in the U.S. went into bankruptcy liquidation, and Signature Bank was also shut down due to "systemic risk." The crisis continued to spread, and on March 19, Switzerland's largest bank, UBS Group, announced its acquisition of the embattled Credit Suisse.

In the midst of this volatile financial environment, how can one protect the safety of their funds?

On March 20, 2023, the China General Chamber of Commerce - Washington State (CCCWA) hosted an in-person financial seminar. The event was led by CCCWA board member ICBC USA, which analyzed recent hot-button financial events and policies, and provided an overview of account service solutions.

The lecture reviewed the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, analyzing the underlying causes of the event and its impact on the global economy. From the perspective of safeguarding funds, it also covered key aspects of Federal Deposit Insurance (FDIC) coverage, including the scope of protection, insurance limits, and how to choose a bank.

The lecture also introduced the service features of ICBC USA: ICBC USA holds a Standard & Poor's global rating of A-, and its professional service team of over 300 local employees provides bilingual support in Chinese and English. Currently, its interest rates are more competitive than those of major U.S. domestic banks, offering individual checking accounts with an annual percentage yield (APY) of 3.5% and corporate checking accounts with up to 3.7% APY. The bank places a strong emphasis on risk management to ensure the safety and stability of client funds.

ICBC USA currently offers a range of specialized services:

  • Cross-border inbound wire transfers for corporate accounts – "ICBC Express" service with zero handling fees;

  • Corporate cash management services – enabling convenient remote check deposits and small-value payments;

  • Personal credit cards – available without an SSN, accepting domestic (Chinese) credit history, with both VISA and UnionPay card networks accepted;

  • Personal mortgage loans – available without an SSN, accepting domestic (Chinese) credit history, pay stubs, and financial assets;

    • Maximum loan-to-value ratio: 70%;

    • Maximum loan amount: $3.5 million USD;

  • Student checking accounts – designed for international students, can be opened before arriving in the U.S., allowing for direct remittances and tuition/fee payments.

items.body_en:
Professor Jie Liu – a leading figure in the field of immune rehabilitation and reconstruction for cancer prevention and treatment, a national-level candidate of the New Century Hundred, Thousand, and Ten Thousand Talents Program, a recipient of the Special Government Allowance of the State Council, and a Changjiang Scholar Distinguished Professor – delivered a public lecture in Seattle back in 2018 titled "Immune Reconstruction and Cancer Prevention and Treatment." In that lecture, in addition to introducing the latest scientific research and clinical advances in early warning and intervention of precancerous lesions and precision cancer therapy, he also shared practical, easy-to-follow methods for enhancing immunity in daily life to prevent cancer and improve overall physical health and function.

Many attendees, particularly busy professionals with high work stress, reported significant benefits from the lecture. They subsequently passed on these health concepts to those around them, and many have since benefited from that public lecture.

At the request of the community, the Chamber has once again invited Professor Liu to deliver an insightful lecture on "Immunity and Health" on May 9 (Beijing Time). In addition to presenting the latest scientific research and clinical progress in precision cancer treatment, this lecture will also specifically address effective ways to boost immunity after recovery from COVID-19. This event will be held both in-person and online; please reserve your seat in advance.

Jie Liu, M.D., Ph.D., Professor, Chief Physician, Ph.D. Supervisor

  • Director of the Institute of Digestive Diseases, Fudan University

  • Director of the Department of Gastroenterology, Huashan Hospital Affiliated with Fudan University

  • Director of the Institute of Immunophenotyping, Shanghai International Institute for Human Phenome Research

  • Principal Investigator of the "Innovative Research Group" on Novel Immunotherapy Strategies

  • "Changjiang Scholar" Distinguished Professor

  • Recipient of the Special Government Allowance of the State Council

  • Leader of the Strategic Innovation Team for High-Level Higher Education Institutions in Shanghai

Research Focus: Immunorehabilitation and immune reconstitution strategies.

  • Established an assessment and intervention system for immunosenescence and biological aging.

  • Pioneered novel non-invasive diagnostic (liquid biopsy) methods based on epigenetic modifications.

  • Developed comprehensive disease diagnosis and treatment strategies based on immune homeostasis.

  • Constructed the fourth-generation secretory CAR-T targeting solid tumors, achieving a breakthrough in CAR-T immunotherapy for solid tumors.

刘杰教授（免疫力康复及重建肿瘤预防及治疗领域的领军人物、新世纪百千万人才工程“国家级”人选、国务院“特殊政府津贴”获得者、长江学者特聘教授），早在2018年就在西雅图做过题为“免疫力重建及肿瘤防治”的公益演讲，演讲中除了介绍癌前病变早期预警及干预、癌症精准治疗的最新科研及临床进展外，还讲述了在日常生活中如何通过简单易行的方式增强免疫力，预防癌症，增强身体机能和健康。

众多听众，尤其是工作压力大、工作繁忙的商务人士在讲座后反馈受益匪浅，后续大家又把这些健康理念传递给身边的人，很多人因那场公益讲座而受益。

应大家要求，商会再次邀请刘杰教授在北京时间5月9日带来精彩的“免疫力与健康”讲座，除了介绍癌症精准治疗的最新科研及临床进展、此次讲座还会有针对性地增加关于感染新冠康复后有效提高免疫力的方式等内容，此次活动为线上线下同时进行，请提前预约座位。

刘杰，医学博士，教授，主任医师，博士生导师，复旦大学消化病研究所所长，附属华山医院消化科主任；上海国际人类表型组研究院免疫表型研究所所长，免疫治疗新策略“创新研究群体”负责人， “长江学者”特聘教授，及“杰出青年基金”获得者；百千万人才工程“国家级”人选；国务院特殊政府津贴获得者；，复旦大学免疫学系教授，及代谢研究院和遗传学系教授，上海肿瘤药物工程研究中心主任；上海双一流免疫交叉科学创新研究院负责人；上海高水平高等院校创新战略团队负责人；上海市优秀学科带头人；上海市领军人才。研究方向为免疫康复及重建策略；。建立了免疫衰老及生物年龄评估及干预体系；创立了基于表观基因修饰的无创诊断（液体活检）新方法；开展了基于免疫稳态的疾病综合诊疗新策略；构建了第四代针对实体瘤的新型分泌型CART，使实体瘤的CART免疫治疗获得突破。开展了基于人工智能的肿瘤个体化新抗原疫苗研究。在Nature 临床实践肿瘤发表的临床病例研究被推举为临床医师继续医学教育教材（CME）。先后发表SCI论文150余篇，包括Cell， Nature 子刊等，申报及获发明专利15项，获国家科技进步一等奖等奖项。

items.title_en: Event Recap: Safety Seminar Co-Hosted by CCCWA and the Bellevue Police Department Concludes Successfully
items.title_zh: 活动回顾：CCCWA与贝尔维尤市警察局联合主办的安全讲座成功落幕
items.body_en: On May 31, 2022, the safety seminar co-hosted by the China General Chamber of Commerce - Washington State (CCCWA) and the Bellevue Police Department was successfully held. The Bellevue Police Department deployed a strong team of nine officers and safety experts to participate in this event. They addressed more than 30 safety questions raised by the audience on everyday work and life topics, including how to use weapons, how to improve self-defense capabilities, how to report emergencies quickly and effectively, and how to identify fake police officers. The presentation focused particularly on security issues of concern to business professionals, such as crime prevention measures that business owners can take on a regular basis, what to do if a store is robbed, and crime prevention strategies for office buildings, apartment complexes, and surrounding areas. The event drew a large audience, with active participation and a lively atmosphere throughout. The seminar featured a well-paced agenda, and the topics discussed were closely related to everyday life and work. The officers and safety experts provided highly practical and actionable answers, which were widely praised. When the final question was asked—"What would Bellevue police do if a school shooting occurred?"—Assistant Chief Popochock replied, "We will rush into the school. We will take the bullets ourselves, rather than letting them hit our children." The audience was deeply moved, and many left messages expressing gratitude to the officers for protecting the community and for delivering such a practical and informative seminar. After the event, many attendees remarked that the session was not only highly beneficial to the audience but also greatly helpful in building strong connections and trust between the police and the community. They felt safer living and working in Bellevue and took greater pride in our city. Police Chief Wendell Shirley attended the event and delivered opening remarks. The event was moderated by PIO Meeghan Black. Ms. Lili Lyu, the current President of CCCWA, expressed the chamber's deep gratitude to the Bellevue Police Department for sending a strong delegation. She also extended special thanks to the co-organizers, including Seattle Immigration Home, Seattle Real Estate Investment Club, Seattle Entrepreneurship Association, and Sunshine Youth Education and Development Foundation.

items.body_en:
Event Recap: CCCWA Restaurant Industry Forum

Tian Hui, President of Studio 19 Architects
Architect Tian Hui shared insights from the perspectives of urban planning and architectural design, noting that as urban zoning improves, the demand for dining establishments in cities is also increasing. He highlighted the mutually beneficial relationship between the restaurant industry and commercial real estate, emphasizing that the growth of the restaurant sector is closely tied to urban development.

Larry Eu, CEO of Great Earth Realty
Larry shared experience and advice on changes in commercial real estate investment trends, the selection of storefront locations for medium- and long-term development of restaurant enterprises, and negotiation and signing strategies for restaurant tenants in lease agreements.

Michelle Lei, General Manager of Chowbus Inc. Seattle Region
Michelle shared market insights derived from analyzing marketing and consumer data of restaurant businesses and customers. She noted that Chinese cuisine is steadily expanding its non-Asian customer base, and that brand recognition and food quality are key to boosting sales and broadening the customer pool.

Jason Huang, Seattle Area Manager of LIUYISHOU HOT POT
Drawing on over 30 years of experience in restaurant business management, Jason summarized the opportunities and challenges faced by the Chinese restaurant industry during the pandemic. He shared comprehensive operational expertise in areas such as business management, product standardization, cost structure, service standard controls, and key evaluation points for franchise partnerships.

David Li, Marketing Manager of Happy Lamb Hot Pot
From the perspective of building a new restaurant brand, David shared how new brands balanced government requirements and consumer demands during the pandemic. He provided a detailed analysis of strategies for expanding into the North American consumer market, brand marketing plans, product standardization and quality control, and potential future investment and expansion directions.

Cai Qing, Attorney at Cai & Associates
Attorney Cai Qing shared legal insights on restaurant franchise models, government review and approval processes, and lease agreements for restaurant spaces, summarizing relevant experience from a legal standpoint.

The participating guests engaged in in-depth discussions and exchanges, sharing experiences and exploring future development trends in the restaurant industry. CCCWA hopes that this forum provided an efficient and high-quality platform for communication and collaboration among restaurant businesses, investors interested in the restaurant industry, and related industry professionals. The goal was to help restaurant enterprises navigate the challenging pandemic period and to spark a new wave of investment in the restaurant industry in the near future.

The forum was moderated by Michelle Zou, Founder of Pacific Consulting. Ms. Lili Lyu, President of CCCWA, and Ms. Man Wang, Vice President of WSCRC (Washington State China Relations Council), attended the forum and delivered remarks on behalf of the hosting organizations.

items.title_en: Event Preview: Seminar on the Best Pathways for International Students to Stay in the U.S.!

items.body_en:
Time flies, and graduation season is coming to an end. Have you made your post-graduation plans to stay in the U.S. in advance? This seminar on the best pathways for international students to remain in the U.S. is jointly hosted by the China General Chamber of Commerce - Washington State (CCCWA) and Cao Law Group on September 1 (U.S. time) / September 2 (Beijing time). The event is designed to provide support and assistance to international students who wish to stay in the U.S., analyzing various options from different perspectives to help you choose a more suitable path.

Event Content Preview

NIW (National Interest Waiver)
The NIW, also known as the advanced-degree professional/exceptional ability immigrant visa, requires applicants to qualify under EB-2 (professionals with advanced degrees or exceptional ability) and meet the NIW standards. Applicants may file directly with USCIS without the need for a U.S. employer sponsor. The process is streamlined, often approved within months, and allows for self-petition.

EB-5 (New Law, No Backlog, Concurrent Filing)
The latest EB-5 legislation signed by President Biden in March 2022 reserves 3,200 visa numbers for three categories of "set-aside projects" with no backlog. Eligible applicants in the U.S. can concurrently file Form I-526 and Form I-485 to adjust status. International students can directly apply for EB-5 set-aside projects and, upon receiving their EAD work permit, begin working without going through the H-1B lottery—resolving the challenges of H-1B visa difficulty and long waiting periods.

IEP (International Entrepreneur Parole Program)
The IEP allows foreign entrepreneurs to create more jobs through their business ideas. Entrepreneurs may initially receive a 30-month parole period and have the right to work for their own startup. Each startup may have up to 1–3 international students/entrepreneurs obtain immigration status. The requirements for the number of jobs created and investment amount are relatively low.

Startup (OPT Entrepreneurship)
F-1 students on OPT may start their own businesses. As long as they can prove they have a business license, are engaged in a business related to their field of study, and comply with immigration laws, they may participate in the establishment and operation of the venture. There are many specific operational details and considerations, so consulting a qualified attorney is strongly recommended.

Other Options
Other pathways such as the O-1 visa are also available.

About Cao Law Group

Cao Law Group is an experienced immigration and business law firm. Its primary practice areas include:

  • Immigration: Investment visas, EB-1 extraordinary ability, National Interest Waiver (NIW), employment-based immigration, family-based immigration, various work visas, appeals, and litigation.

  • Business Law: General corporate counsel, e-commerce consulting, business formation, share transfers, real estate transactions and transfers.

  • Litigation: Enforcement of Chinese judgments in the U.S.

The firm also partners with the Seattle Business Center to provide remote notary services (domestic and international), three-level authentication, and virtual office services.

时光飞逝，毕业季即将结束，是否已经提前做好留美规划。此次由CCCWA华盛顿州中国总商会、曹霄鹤律师事务所于美国时间9月1日（北京时间9月2日）联合举办国际留学生最佳留美方案讲座。旨在为有意向留在美国的留学生提供帮助和支持，从不同角度分析一些留美方式，帮助选择更适合的留美方案。

活动内容预告：

NIW(国家利益豁免移民)

NIW国家利益豁免移民也称高级技术人才移民，申请人须符合EB-2（具有高等学位的专业人士/特殊能力专业人士）资格，并达到NIW（国家利益豁免）标准，可对移民局直接提出移民申请。审批流程简洁，通常数月即可获批，且不需要美国雇主担保，可自行申请。

EB-5（新法案、无排期、双递交）

2022年3月拜登总统签署的最新EB-5法案中，为三类“签证预留项目”预留3200个免排期名额。可以在美国境内同时递交I-526申请和I-485转换身份申请。国际留学生可直接申请预留项目的EB-5，在拿到EAD工卡后即可工作，无需H1B抽签，解决了留学生想通过H1B留美抽签难、等待排期长的问题。

IER(国际企业家特许项目)

IEP允许外籍创业者将商业理念创造更多的就业机会。创业者首次将获得30个月的居留期限，并有权为自己创业的公司工作。每个初创企业可以有1-3个国际留学生/企业家获得移民身份。对于创造的就业机会数量和投资金额要求不高。

Startup(OPT身份创业)

F-1留学生在OPT期间可自行创业，在能够证明自己拥有营业执照并从事与学生学位课程相关的业务和遵守移民法的情况下参与企业的创立经营。具体操作和注意事项较多，需咨询专业律师。

还有其他选择，例如O1等等。


曹霄鹤律师事务所简介

曹霄鹤律师事务所是一家经验丰富的移民商务律师事务所。主要专业领域包括：【移民】投资移民，杰出人才移民，国家利益豁免，科技职业移民，亲属移民，各类工作签证，上诉及诉讼；【商务法律】常年法律顾问，电商咨询，公司成立，股份转让，房产交易过户；【诉讼】中国判决的美国执行。 同时联手《西雅图商务中心》，提供：海内外远程视频公证服务，三级认证，远程办公室服务。

items.body_en:
Event Recap | CCCWA and East West Bank Host Seminar on U.S. and Global Financial and Real Estate Markets

The online seminar on the latest insights and outlook for U.S. and global financial and real estate markets, co-hosted by the China General Chamber of Commerce - Washington State (CCCWA) and East West Bank, concluded successfully on November 10 (U.S. time) / November 11 (China time). The event featured an insightful live presentation by Dr. Hsu Chung-Hsiang, Chief Economist of East West Bank, covering the current U.S. financial markets, government interest rate hikes, inflation, and future real estate trends.

Key Takeaways

1. U.S. Macroeconomic Overview

How long will U.S. interest rate hikes continue?
The U.S. is likely to maintain high interest rates for a relatively extended period. Although inflation has dropped from 9% to 4%, roughly 3% of the previous 9% inflation was driven by the Russia-Ukraine war (energy and food prices), and another 3% stemmed from supply chain disruptions when many Chinese factories were unable to operate at full capacity late last year. Therefore, the decline in U.S. inflation is not solely the result of rate hikes; over time, inflation would naturally moderate.

The U.S. is currently facing a structural labor shortage. Unemployment is at a historic low, and wages are rising. Due to the pandemic, many Americans around age 60 chose to retire after working from home for three years, while younger workers increasingly prefer gig work over returning to traditional employment models.

No significant rate cuts are expected in 2024. It may not be until 2025, when a new president takes office (with a strong possibility of Trump being re-elected after a gap), that we might see substantial rate cuts, potentially triggering bull markets in both stocks and real estate.

2. How long will high interest rates persist, and what is the impact on real estate and the stock market?

For now, it is unwise to be overly optimistic about 2024 or to chase market highs blindly. The stock market may still be bottoming out. High rates (around 5%–5.5%) could persist for another year or more. Long-term bonds may be a good income option at current levels—there's no need to bet heavily on rate cuts, as that carries significant risk.

In the long run, a new president will likely lower rates, given that U.S. fiscal revenue may barely cover interest payments alone. A new administration would want to avoid fiscal constraints, and lower rates would likely ignite a bull market in both stocks and real estate. In the short term, however, sharp fluctuations are unlikely, and expectations for rate cuts should be tempered.

3. Future Development of China's Economy

Many economists worry about China following Japan's path—a real estate bubble leading to three decades of economic stagnation. However, while high property prices in China are a social issue, they have not yet escalated into a systemic economic crisis. The "Japanification" narrative may be somewhat conspiratorial.

The Chinese government has been actively deleveraging. Individual homebuyers in China carry relatively low leverage—the leverage is mainly concentrated among developers. Early on, the government introduced the "Three Red Lines" policy to transfer non-compliant, over-leveraged developers to lower-leverage companies, reducing uncontrollable risks and the potential for a real estate-triggered crisis.

Chinese households tend to store wealth in real estate, Americans in stocks, and Indians in gold. If the Chinese government can successfully shift household savings from property to primary and secondary capital markets, it could be more effective for long-term development.

China currently has low inflation. Although local government finances are under pressure, central government fiscal revenue remains sound, allowing for monetary easing without triggering inflation.

On the international front, China's primary goal is to issue debt and enhance the renminbi's global influence, aiming for RMB internationalization as a "second U.S. dollar." Success in issuing sovereign debt could also boost China's A-share markets and the broader economy.

Q&A Session

Q: Is now a good time to bottom-fish in the U.S. housing market?
Dr. Hsu: Single-family homes have not been significantly affected by the rate hikes, nor is there strong selling pressure. It's not easy to buy at low prices, and we don't need to worry about a crash similar to 2007–2008.

Q: What impact will the Israel-Hamas war have on the global economy?
Dr. Hsu: The most immediate effect is added upward pressure on inflation. If the conflict draws in the broader Middle East, energy prices could be severely affected. Negatively, it would prolong U.S. inflation; positively, it could ease U.S.-China tensions.

Q: Is now a good time to invest in AI?
Dr. Hsu: AI's current market valuation is driven more by expectations than by actual applications. In the short term, it won't fundamentally change daily life. Similar to the internet, major breakthroughs often come in the second or third wave. AI is definitely a long-term trend (10–20 years), but short-term risks are high, and the industry is still far from full maturity.

Q: Given the current global environment, how should we think about medium- to long-term asset allocation? What is the appropriate ratio between developed and emerging markets?
Dr. Hsu: Historically, developed and emerging markets tend to alternate in outperformance. Over the past decade, developed markets have led with higher returns. In the next decade, emerging markets are more likely to take the lead. Why? Price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios are relatively low by historical standards, underestimating emerging markets' growth potential, while developed markets have higher P/E ratios. Market cycles suggest greater potential in emerging markets. Additionally, over the past five years, amid U.S.-China competition, many resource-rich smaller countries have grown rapidly, driving up raw material prices.

Q: What is the outlook for U.S. real estate?
Dr. Hsu: 2024 is expected to be largely range-bound. A new real estate bull market likely won't emerge until after the new president takes office in 2025 and introduces new policies. For now, buyers should focus on school-district homes and personal needs.

Q: What is your stock market outlook for 2024–2025?
Dr. Hsu: 2024 will likely see continued volatility. A conservative approach is advisable, as there may not be a sustained upward theme in the near term.

由CCCWA华盛顿州中国总商会携手华美银行于美国时间11月10日（中国11月11日）举办的美国及全球金融和房地产市场最新解读与展望线上讲座活动圆满结束。本次活动由主讲人华美银行首席经济学家许仲翔博士带来了目前美国金融市场、政府加息、通货膨胀以及未来房地产走势等的精彩现场演讲。


重点内容分享 

美国宏观经济的情况


1、美国升息会升多久

美国高利息水平会维持相对的久，虽然通货膨胀率从9%降至4%，但是之前9%的通货膨胀率里面的3%是俄乌战争造成的，从能源，粮食方面引发的通货膨胀，另外3%的原因是去年尾端，中国很多工厂不能全产能出货，导致的通货膨胀。

所以美国通货膨胀率的下降，并不是升息带来的影响，时间拉的够长，通货膨胀率会自然而然下降。

美国目前面临的是结构性劳动力衰退，失业率历史新低，工资薪酬高涨，疫情影响下，很多60岁左右的美国人，在居家工作3年之后直接选择退休，而年轻人更多选择打零工，不愿意重新返回传统的工作模式。

2024年预计不会有大幅降息的情况，可能要到2025年新任总统履职或者上任之后，川普有很大几率跳届之后再次当选，会大幅压低利率，带来股市和房地产的牛市行情。


2、高利率水平会维持多久，对房地产，对股市的影响

目前来看，不要对于2024年盲目乐观，不要盲目追高，股市仍旧有筑底的可能性。可能维持高利率还要1年多，5%-5.5%的利率，长债收入也是个不错的选择，不需要去赌降息，风险较大。

长期来看，新上任的总统必然会降低利率，如今美国每年的财政收入光偿还利息可能都会存在问题，新上任总统不会让自己没有钱花，利率下降，股市和房市肯定会带来一波牛市。但是短期来看，不会出现剧烈波动，大家对于降息不用期望过高。


中国经济未来发展


现在有很多经济学家担心中国经济走向日本化，日本房地产泡沫化带来日本30年的经济衰退，中国房地产的贵是个社会矛盾问题，并没有上升到社会经济问题，日本化的经济走向也是一种阴谋论。

政府一直非常积极的在去杠杆化，中国人本身购买房产的杠杆是很低的，杠杆主要集中在开发商，第一和第二时间政府发布三条红线把很多不合规，杠杆过高的房地产商转移给杠杆低的公司，降低不可控风险，降低房地产引爆的风险。

中国人喜欢存钱在房地产，美国人喜欢存钱在股票，印度人喜欢存钱在黄金，中国政府如果能够让大家不把钱存在房地产，而是把钱投到一级市场和二级市场，那么对中国长期发展是更有效的。

中国目前处于通胀水平低情况，虽然说地方财政不是特别好，但是中国中央财政收入较好，可以通过印钞票放水促进经济，而不会引起通膨的情况。

中国在国际上主要还是想发债，提高人民币在国际上的影响力，使人民币国际化，成为国际“第二美元”。中国发债成功，也将会促进A股股市和经济。


线上问答


Q：关于美国房产市场抄底？

许：美国Single Family并没有受到这次升息的影响，也没有售出压力，如果想要低价买入还是不太容易实现的，也不需要担心类似于07,08年房价大跌的情况出现。

Q：巴以战争对于世界经济有什么影响？

许：巴以战争带来最明显的影响是，它会让通货膨胀的压力持续，如果中东把整个中欧拉进来，对于能源的影响是显著的。从负面来讲，会延续美国的通货膨胀，从正面来讲，会缓和中美之间的关系。

Q：现在是一个很好的时间买AI吗？

许：AI市场预期的比重大于实际应用的比重，短期内并不会对生活有本质性改变，类似于Internet，往往崛起都是在第二波，第三波，AI绝对是未来10年，20年的趋势，但是短期来看风险性太高，距离产业真正成熟还有一定时间。

Q：在现在的全球环境下，如何思考资产中长期配置？发达市场和新兴市场的配置比例？

许：如果看大方向，发达市场和新兴市场是风水轮流转，在过去10年里面，发达市场占据主流，获利较高，后面10年，回到新兴市场的概率较高。

原因是市盈率（P/E）相对历史低点，低估了新兴市场的成长率，发达市场市盈率较高，根据市场的周期性来说新兴市场的潜力更大。

再者，在过去5年，中国和美国角力的过程中，很多拥有资源的中小国家发展很快，原物料的价格也哄抬上来。

Q：美国未来房地产趋势

许：2024年预计是振荡为主，还是需要等2025年新总统上台之后的新政策，才可能会有新一波房地产牛市，大家现在可以主要以学区房和自身需求为主。

Q：2024-2025年股票走势分析

许：2024年大概率是振荡，以比较保守的态度购买，预计不会有长期上涨的题材。

The China General Chamber of Commerce - Washington State (CCCWA), in partnership with East West Bank, invites you to a seminar on Property Ownership and Estate Planning. Join us to learn key strategies for handling real estate title in estate planning. The seminar will be conducted in Chinese, with on-site English interpretation provided. A light meal will be served by East West Bank. Seats are limited—please register early.

Presentation Content

For Chinese Americans, a house is often their most valuable asset and a major component of family wealth. Over the past decade, as the Seattle area has become one of the top destination cities for Chinese Americans residing, studying, working, traveling, doing business, and investing in the United States, the number of home purchases by Chinese Americans in the Seattle area—both for personal residence and investment purposes—has surged. It is now common for families to own multiple properties. However, when purchasing a home, many buyers give insufficient thought to critical issues such as: who should hold title, in what form of ownership the title should be held, how to change title holders, how marriage and divorce affect property ownership, how the form of ownership impacts capital gains tax and gift tax upon sale or gifting of the property, and how to transfer the property to heirs after death while avoiding probate. Attorney Cai Qing will use real-life case studies to discuss the relationship between property ownership and family wealth holding, tax savings, and succession planning, as well as the significant implications of these factors.

items.body_en:
The current changes in the international landscape have brought both tremendous opportunities and significant challenges for Chinese multinational enterprises operating in the United States. The explosive popularity of TikTok in North America, the IPO filing of fast-fashion brand Shein in the U.S., and the fact that Pinduoduo's cross-border platform Temu has become the most downloaded shopping app in the U.S. market all demonstrate the strength of Chinese companies in "going global." Along this journey, every enterprise will undoubtedly face legal, operational, and tax challenges. To this end, the China General Chamber of Commerce - Washington State has specially invited four experts to share insights and discuss topics including intellectual property protection, human resources management, immigration risk planning, and commercial transaction trends for multinational enterprises, with the goal of safeguarding the growth of Chinese multinational companies in the United States.

Cao Xiaohe (Stephanie Cao)
Founder of Cao Law Group (USA) and Founder of the International Law Society

Topics
Navigating immigration policies and changes, and designing strategies for cross-border personnel transfers and U.S. recruitment for multinational enterprises.

Bio
Ms. Cao Xiaohe holds a B.A. in International Economic Law from China University of Political Science and Law and a J.D. from the United States. She is licensed to practice in both China and the U.S. With 18 years of dedicated focus on U.S. immigration law, she has represented numerous regional centers and hundreds of investors in direct investment immigration projects, assisted corporate executives and skilled professionals in relocating to the U.S., developed immigration strategies for individuals with extraordinary abilities and national interest waiver applicants in light of U.S. policies, and designed comprehensive short- and long-term work and visitor visa plans for enterprises. She has been a long-standing immigration expert guest on U.S. Chinese-language radio and Seattle Chinese Radio for over a decade, and also hosts the "Attorney Cao's Advice Column" as a featured expert.

hu Shaobin (Shaobin Zhu)
Partner at Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP (USA)

Topics
How to strengthen market competitiveness and reduce legal risks through intellectual property, and how to respond to potential and ongoing IP litigation.

Bio
Mr. Zhu Shaobin is a Partner at Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP, Co-Leader of the firm's China Intellectual Property Practice, and Head of the China IP Team. He focuses on the technology sector and provides legal services in U.S. district court IP litigation (including patents, trade secrets, trademarks, domain names, and copyrights), U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) Section 337 investigations, client counseling, IP licensing, legal opinions, patent prosecution, data privacy, cybersecurity, open-source software strategy, and international arbitration. Mr. Zhu has helped dozens of Chinese clients successfully resolve their IP disputes in the United States. By employing countermeasures before the U.S. Patent Office, in courts, and in China, as well as through strategic negotiations, he has helped Chinese clients mitigate losses and achieve favorable outcomes.

Ni Xuanlu
Partner and Americas Lead for the International China Market, Vialto Partners

Topics
An overview of how Chinese companies can strategically plan ahead to improve their success rate in going global, and how to mitigate risks.

Bio
Ms. Ni Xuanlu is a Partner at Vialto Partners (formerly PwC's Global Mobility practice) and serves as the Americas Lead for the firm's International China Market. Since 2002, Ms. Ni has focused on providing global human resources, tax planning, and overseas business expansion services to major multinational corporations and global enterprise clients. With nearly 20 years of extensive hands-on experience, she has also advised C-suite ultra-high-net-worth individuals of global giants. Ms. Ni holds a bachelor's degree from Renmin University of China and an MBA from the University of Toronto. She is a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) licensed in the State of Washington, USA.

Shen Han
Attorney at Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati (USA)

Topics
Trends in U.S. capital market activities and commercial transactions for multinational enterprises

Bio
Ms. Shen Han is licensed to practice in both the U.S. (Washington State and California) and China. She primarily represents corporations and investment institutions in financings, M&A, reorganizations, public listings, patent licensing and R&D collaborations, energy tax equity financings, and other transactions, participating in over 200 deals per year on average. She holds a B.A. in Law and an LL.M. in International Law from Peking University, as well as a J.D. and an LL.M. in Taxation (dual degree) from the University of Washington School of Law, where she graduated with the highest honors (Order of the Coif).

当前国际形势的变化为中资跨国企业在美国发展带来了巨大的机遇与挑战。抖音国际版TikTok在北美爆火，快时尚品牌Shein已申请美国上市，拼多多跨境平台Temu已经成为美国市场下载量最高的购物应用，都说明了中国企业“走出去”的实力。在这“走出去”的过程中，任何企业无疑都会面临法律、运营与税务方面的挑战。为此，华盛顿州中国总商会特地邀请了四位专家，就跨国企业的知识产权保护、人力资源管理、移民风险规划、商业交易趋势进行分享与探讨，希望为中资跨国企业在美国发展保驾护航！

曹霄鹤

美国曹霄鹤律师事务所创始人、国际法律联盟（International Law Society ）创始人


主讲内容

掌握移民政策及变化，设计跨国企业人员调动与美国招募


曹霄鹤律师是中国政法大学国际经济法学士，美国法学博士，中美两国执业资格。18年专注美国移民法律，代表多家区域中心和直接投资移民项目数百个投资人移民，帮助企业高管和技术人才落户美国，结合美国政策为特殊人才，国家利益豁免人才制定移民方案，为企业做长短期工作及访问签证统一规划。美国中文电台和西雅图中文电台十几年来移民专家嘉宾，曹律师信箱专家主持。

朱韶斌

美国摩根路易斯律师事务所合伙人


主讲内容

如何用知识产权增强市场竞争力，降低法律风险，以及如何应对潜在和发生的知识产权诉讼


朱韶斌律师是美国摩根路易斯律师事务所 (Morgan Lewis) 合伙人，中国知识产权业务的联合负责人以及中国知识产权团队的负责人，专注于科技行业，就美国地区法院的知识产权诉讼(包括专利、商业秘密、商标、域名和版权)和美国国际贸易委员会(ITC)337 条款调查、客户咨询、知识产权许可、法律意见书、专利申请、数据隐私、网络安全、开源软件策略、和国际仲裁等事宜提供法律服务。朱律师已经帮助几十位中国客户成功解决了他们在美国的知 识产权纠纷，通过在美国专利局、法院、及中国采取反制措施和实施策略性地谈 判，成功帮助中国客户降低了损失，取得了有利的结果。

倪轩璐

纬迩拓国际中国市场美洲区负责人


主讲内容

概述中企如何提前规划布局来提高出海成功率以及如何规避风险


倪轩璐是纬迩拓（前普华永道国际派遣业务部）合伙人和国际中国市场美洲区负责人。倪女士从2002年起专注于为国际著名大型跨国公司和全球巨头企业提供全球人力资源，税务筹划和海外业务拓展方面的相关服务。积累了近20年的丰富实战经验（包括为全球巨头企业的总裁级超高净值人士提供相关咨询服务）。倪女士拥有中国人民大学本科学位和多伦多大学工商管理硕士学位。她是美国华盛顿州注册会计师（CPA）。

沈 寒

美国威尔逊律师事务所律师

主讲内容

跨国企业在美国的资本市场活动和商业交易趋势交流


沈寒律师具有在中美两国执业的经验，是美国华盛顿州与加州以及中国注册律师。沈寒律师主要代表企业和投资机构参与融资、并购、重组、上市、专利许可与研发合作、能源税惠权益筹资等各类交易，平均每年参与200多起交易。沈寒律师为北京大学法学学士、国际法学硕士，美国华盛顿大学法学博士、税法进阶硕士 (双学位)，并获得美国法学博士学位最高毕业荣誉。

items.title_zh: CCCWA联合锦天城律师事务所圆满举办“中美投资与贸易新趋势新春座谈会”
items.body_en:
On the afternoon of February 19, 2024 (local time in Seattle), the Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State (CCCWA), in partnership with member firm AllBright Law Offices' Seattle office, co-hosted the Chinese New Year Symposium on New Trends in U.S.-China Investment and Trade. This event also marked the inaugural session of the CCCWA Members Salon for 2024.

Founded in 1999, AllBright Law Offices is a comprehensive law firm offering one-stop legal services with industry-leading strengths in its core practice areas. Originating in Shanghai, AllBright has established 30 offices across 24 cities in China—including Beijing, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou—as well as in Hong Kong, London, Seattle, Singapore, and Tokyo. The Seattle office was officially registered on July 15, 2020, with the mission of supporting AllBright's clients in North America and representing a significant step in the firm's global strategic expansion.

The symposium was co-hosted by Ms. Lili Lv, President of CCCWA, and Attorney Wang Qinghua, Senior Partner at AllBright and Head of the Seattle office.

During the keynote session, Attorney Wang Qinghua, the head of the Seattle office, delivered a presentation titled "New Trends in U.S.-China Bilateral Direct Investment and Case Studies." Attorney Wang provided a comprehensive analysis of key aspects of bilateral direct investment, including total investment volumes, major industry sectors, regional distribution, and representative transactions. Drawing on two detailed case studies, she offered the audience an in-depth examination of the current landscape of U.S.-China bilateral direct investment. Sidong Zhu, Senior Partner at AllBright Law Offices and a member of the Management Committee of its Seattle office, drew on his years of practical experience to share insights with the audience on how Chinese-backed enterprises can raise capital in the United States through IPOs. Yigang Jiang, Senior Partner at AllBright Law Offices and a member of the Management Committee of its Seattle office, delivered remarks highlighting the firm's background and overview. He also introduced the future development plans for the Seattle office and expressed a strong desire to foster greater exchanges with U.S.-based companies and to strengthen ties with the Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State in the future. The guest speakers delivered inspiring and insightful presentations, sharing their valuable experiences with the audience. The corporate representatives in attendance were highly engaged and showed great enthusiasm for the topics discussed during the seminar. They exchanged views on cross-border investment between China and the U.S., and explored strategies for Chinese enterprises to better leverage the U.S. market for growth and development. The seminar concluded with great success.

本次座谈会由华盛顿州中国总商会会长吕莉莉女士和锦天城高级合伙人、西雅图办公室负责人王清华律师联合主持。

items.body_en:
On the afternoon of March 10 (U.S. time), the Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State (CCCWA) hosted a women entrepreneurs' gathering titled "Spring in the Emerald City – Elegance in Togetherness" at the penthouse clubhouse of the Emerald luxury condominiums in downtown Seattle.

The event was co-hosted by Ms. Lili Lv, President of CCCWA, and Michelle Zou, a Microsoft Global Trainer & Talent Coach and a certified instructor of the HAS (Happiness Studies Academy). Michelle shared insights from Dr. Tal Ben-Shahar's happiness studies and introduced practical, easy-to-apply methods for incorporating happiness into daily life. Through an engaging and fun interactive game, she helped break the ice among attendees, encouraging the women entrepreneurs to reflect on their entrepreneurial journeys and life experiences, and to deepen their mutual understanding.

The sponsor and featured speaker of this event was Nini Wu, a Private Bank Wealth Planning Advisor currently at Morgan Stanley. She is a CFA charterholder with over a decade of experience in wealth and asset management across both China and the United States. She shared her perspectives on the current state and trends of various investment products—including real estate, secondary market equities, pre-IPO investments, and digital currencies—as well as her investment philosophy.

Coco Zhu, a Washington State licensed permanent makeup artist and makeup artist, along with Aimi Jiang, a beauty enthusiast in the field of anti-aging medicine, also shared insights on the current state of the medical aesthetics industry, as well as tips on anti-aging and beauty care.

The female entrepreneurs in attendance showed great interest in the topics discussed during the event. The conversation was lively and engaging, covering a wide range of subjects including business management, investment and financial planning, work-life balance, and children's education. Following the session, attendees toured the Emerald Waterfront Condominiums, a project developed by member company Toho USA Real Estate Development, and took a group photo at the clubhouse to commemorate the occasion.

items.body_en:
Due to factors such as immigration policies, educational purposes, investment returns, asset protection, and permanent property rights, a significant proportion of Chinese Americans purchase residential properties in the United States—whether for personal use or as rental investments.

Real estate consistently remains a core component of Chinese American family wealth. However, because U.S. property ownership systems—along with related tax, transfer, gifting, and inheritance laws—differ considerably from those in China, the manner in which U.S. real estate is held and disposed of can have a substantial impact on the growth or erosion of family wealth. To address these critical issues, the organizer has specially arranged this seminar and invited Attorney Alex Cai to provide expert guidance.

Attorney Alex Cai is a practicing attorney in Washington State, providing services to clients on cross-border wealth succession matters. He assists clients in drafting trusts, prenuptial agreements, wills, and financial powers of attorney, and helps with the preparation and recording of Washington State real property transfer documents and registrations.

Topics to Be Covered:

  1. Comparison of property ownership structures between China and the United States

  2. Detailed explanation of property ownership structures in Washington State

  3. Pros and cons of holding property in the name of individuals, spouses, companies, and trusts

  4. How to qualify for Washington State real estate excise tax exemptions upon property transfer

  5. Key considerations when purchasing, holding, selling, gifting, and inheriting Washington State real estate

  6. Property ownership structures to consider when parents provide funds for children's home purchases

  7. Inheritance issues for Washington residents owning in-state and out-of-state properties

items.body_en:
The current shifting international landscape presents both tremendous opportunities and significant challenges for Chinese multinational enterprises expanding in the United States. The explosive popularity of TikTok in North America, the U.S. IPO application of fast-fashion brand Shein, and Pinduoduo's cross-border platform becoming the most-downloaded shopping app in the U.S. market have all set inspiring examples for Chinese companies "going global." However, in the process of expanding abroad, businesses will inevitably face legal challenges. To address these needs, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State has specially invited its General Counsel, Attorney Shirley Cao, to share insights and engage in discussion on immigration planning for multinational enterprises in their global expansion journey.

Featured Speaker: Attorney Shirley Cao

Founder, Law Office of Shirley Cao
Founder, International Law Society


Shirley Cao serves as General Counsel of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State (CCCWA). She holds an LL.B. in International Economic Law from China University of Political Science and Law and a J.D. from the United States, and is licensed to practice in both China and the U.S. With 18 years of dedicated focus on U.S. immigration law, she has represented numerous regional centers and direct investment projects, assisting hundreds of immigrant investors. She has helped corporate executives and skilled professionals relocate to the U.S., developed immigration strategies for individuals with extraordinary ability and those eligible for national interest waivers, and designed comprehensive short- and long-term work and visitor visa plans for businesses. For over a decade, she has served as a guest immigration expert on U.S. Chinese Radio and Seattle Chinese Radio, and as the host of the "Attorney Cao's Advice" column.

Seminar Focus

This seminar aims to share insights and practical advice on immigration policy, business environment, and legal information relevant to immigration planning and U.S. residency. The target audience includes multinational executives, technical experts, investors, entrepreneurs, and professionals across all industries seeking global opportunities.

Mastering Immigration Policy Changes – Strategies for Multinational Workforce Relocation and U.S. Recruitment

In today's globalized business environment, a deep understanding of U.S. immigration options is critical to career success. This seminar provides entrepreneurs, executives, and professionals with comprehensive guidance on pathways to the U.S.—ranging from temporary work visas (such as H-1B, L-1, and O visas) to permanent residency options (including EB-1A, EB-1C, EB-5, PERM, and NIW).

To identify the true owners behind businesses and prevent criminals from using shell companies for money laundering, terrorist financing, and other illegal activities, the U.S. government, under the Corporate Transparency Act (effective January 1, 2024), requires all companies established and registered in the United States to file a Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) report by January 1, 2025.

However, questions surrounding who is responsible for filing, what company information needs to be disclosed, and who should be identified as a beneficial owner have caused considerable confusion and uncertainty.


Speaker Profile:

Attorney Alex Cai is a seasoned practicing attorney in Washington State. He provides professional legal services to numerous cross-border companies and high-net-worth individuals in areas including U.S. corporate matters, investment transactions, and cross-border wealth succession planning.

Attorney Cai will address audience concerns by sharing insights on the following reporting-related questions:

  1. Who is the reporting company?

  2. Who is the beneficial owner?

  3. After the initial filing, is annual compliance reporting required?

  4. What changes require an updated report to be filed?

  5. Will the reported information be made public or shared with other countries?

  6. How should LLCs with "member-managed" versus "manager-managed" structures file their reports?

  7. How should individual shareholders and corporate shareholders in a company file?

  8. How should shares held by a nominee on behalf of others be reported?

  9. How should the company's actual controller file?

  10. How should shares held by a family trust be reported?

  11. How should a company that is wholly owned by an offshore company—which itself is an overseas publicly listed company—file?

  12. How should a company that is owned by a Chinese state-owned enterprise file?

  13. A comparison of reporting requirements between China's Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (effective November 1, 2024) and the U.S. Corporate Transparency Act.

Given that Chinese Americans are actively engaged in business and investment activities in the U.S., and that U.S. companies often have Chinese individual and corporate shareholders, failure to file—or filing incomplete or inaccurate information—could result in significant civil or criminal penalties, as well as negative impacts on the company's reputation, bank loan applications, and normal business operations. To address these critical issues, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State (CCCWA) is hosting this event and has invited Attorney Alex Cai to share his expertise.

Organizer: Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Washington State (CCCWA)

Event Time: December 3, 15:00 – 17:00 (U.S. Time)

Venue: 12509 Bel-Red Rd. #100, Bellevue, WA 98005

为了识别企业背后真实所有者，以防止犯罪分子利用空壳公司洗钱、资助恐怖主义和从事其他非法活动，美国政府根据于2024年1月1日生效的“企业透明法”，要求所有在美国设立和登记公司必须在2025年1月1日前递交受益所有权信息申报报告，即所谓的“BOI Reporting”。


但由谁来申报、需要申报哪些公司信息、以及需要把谁作为受益所有权人申报等问题令人疑虑和困惑。

分享人简介：

蔡清律师为华州资深执业律师

为众多跨境公司和高净值群体在美国公司事务、投资事务、跨境财富传承事务

提供专业服务。


蔡清律师将通过分享回答听众关注问题，包括以下申报问题：


1、谁是申报公司？

2、谁是受益所有权人？

3、初次申报后，是否每年需要合规申报？

4、哪些信息变更时需要递交更新报告？

5、申报信息会被公开吗或被交换给他国吗？

6、LLC公司为“股东管理”或“经理管理”不同公司类型时如何申报？

7、公司中的个人股东和企业股东如何申报？

8、股东为他人代持股权时如何申报？

9、公司实控人如何申报？

10、股权由家庭信托持有时如何申报？

11、公司由境外公司独资持有，而境外公司是境外上市公司时如何申报？

12、公司由中国国有企业持有时，如何申报？

13、于2024年11月1日生效的中国《受益所有人信息管理办法》与美国《企业透明法》申报要求比较。


鉴于华人在美国从事商业和投资活动较普遍，加上美国公司中也往往会有中国个人和企业股东参股，如未申报、申报信息不真实或不完整都将导致重大民事或刑事处罚，以及也会对公司声誉、申请银行贷款产生负面影响并会严重影响公司正常经营活动，华盛顿州中国总商会特此举办本次活动邀请蔡清律师分享他的经验。

items.title_en: CCCWA Real Estate Development and Investment Salon – Session 3: How to Maximize Land Value Under the New HB 1110 and HB 1337 Policies
items.title_zh: CCCWA房地产开发与投资沙龙第三期：如何利用HB1110和HB1337新政最大化土地价值？
items.body_en:
In recent years, Washington State has introduced two landmark housing reform bills—HB 1110 (the Middle Housing Bill) and HB 1337 (the Accessory Dwelling Unit Bill)—aimed at addressing the housing crisis and increasing housing diversity and affordability.

According to projections, Washington State will need to add 1 million new housing units by 2044, with King County alone requiring 340,000 units. HB 1110 mandates that many cities allow a broader range of housing types—such as duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, townhomes, stacked flats, and cottage housing—in areas previously zoned exclusively for single-family homes.

We cordially invite you to join our upcoming seminar this week on "How to Maximize Land Value Under the New HB 1110 and HB 1337 Policies."

This seminar will feature Bili Peng, Founder of 5ft2 Studio Architects, and Alex Yu, Engineer at Merit Engineering, who will provide an in-depth analysis of these two new bills. They will explore how these acts are reshaping Washington State's traditional "single-family home-dominated" residential model, and discuss their far-reaching implications for future development directions, real estate investment, homeowner rights, and the evolution of urban spatial patterns in Washington.

Bili Peng is a registered architect in Washington State. With over 20 years of professional architectural experience, she brings a rich international background to her work. Bili founded 5ft2 Studio Architects in Amsterdam before establishing her practice in Seattle. Today, she focuses on integrating her extensive international design experience into local architectural and interior design projects. Her deep understanding of local building codes and regional culture allows her to bring a unique and thoughtful perspective to every project.

  • Primary areas of expertise: geotechnical engineering consulting and design, water resource management and wastewater treatment design, civil engineering design, and construction project management
